title: Uniform circular motion

draft.title: Uniform circular motion
card: In uniform circular motion, an object moves in a circle at constant speed. Its velocity still changes, because the direction keeps changing.
A change in velocity is an acceleration. So the object accelerates towards the centre of the circle, even though its speed stays the same.
By Newton's second law, this acceleration needs a net force towards the centre. This is the centripetal force: F = mv²/r, where m is mass, v is speed and r is the radius.
Centripetal force is not a new kind of force. It is the name for the net force towards the centre, supplied by tension, gravity, friction or another force.
draft.remember: Circular motion at constant speed means acceleration and net force towards the centre.

a.q: A ball on a string is swung in a horizontal circle at constant speed. Which statement about the ball is correct?
opts: It accelerates towards the centre of the circle
It has zero acceleration because its speed is constant
It accelerates in the direction it is moving
It accelerates away from the centre of the circle
a.why: Velocity includes direction, and the direction keeps changing, so the ball accelerates towards the centre. Zero acceleration is tempting because the speed is constant, but speed is only part of velocity.
a.clue: Velocity has direction as well as speed.

b.q: A 2.0 kg trolley moves at 3.0 m/s in a circle of radius 1.5 m. What is the net force towards the centre?
b.why: F = mv²/r = 2.0 × 3.0² ÷ 1.5 = 12 N. Using v instead of v² gives 4.0 N, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: The speed is squared in the formula.

a.best: It accelerates towards the centre of the circle
